stops.label: Woodbridge (Occoquan)

Prior fast-ferry plans (PRTC M-495) named this exact terminal and never launched.

speed_wake_honesty.rule: Segments flagged speed_constrained:true must render water_min as 'indicative — subject to DC harbor speed rules'. NO crossing-time claims for Georgetown or Navy Yard appear anywhere in copy until regulatory engagement resolves.
constrained_zones: Permanent no-wake zone Memorial Bridge → Chain Bridge (all Georgetown legs)
Strict no-wake, Washington Channel (all Wharf approaches)

speed_wake_honesty.note: A zero-wake hydrofoil does NOT automatically get an exemption from posted speed limits — DC Harbor Patrol/DOEE/USCG engagement required. #1 regulatory workstream.

copy.hero: Your dock becomes a station on a connected water network. Navier is building an employer water network for the DC waterfront — 20-seat electric hydrofoils linking Old Town Alexandria, The Wharf, Georgetown, Navy Yard, and National Harbor, growing to the Pentagon, National Landing (by shuttle), and the Potomac suburbs.

sections.why_dc: DC has the worst traffic congestion of any US metro, a river running straight through its densest job clusters, and a proven precedent: when Metro shut down in 2019, a single Old Town↔Wharf boat carried 5,000 riders a day. Every launch station is an active water-taxi landing today — no new infrastructure needed on day one.
sections.how_it_works: Employers commit seat blocks on a corridor. When a corridor reaches 60–80 committed seats, it launches. Seats are guaranteed, quiet, working commutes on zero-emission electric hydrofoils.
sections.network: Two launch lines — the Monument Line (National Harbor · Old Town Alexandria · The Wharf · Georgetown) and the Capitol Line (Old Town · Navy Yard) — with Old Town Alexandria as the network interchange. Phase 2 and 3 stations render as planned, not promised.
sections.georgetown_positioning: Georgetown is the premium last-mile into a Metro-poor office district — a calm water arrival at Washington Harbour's front door. (No travel-time claims on this leg.)
sections.national_landing: National Landing riders connect via a short branded shuttle from our Daingerfield Island station — a door-to-dock-to-desk trip for the HQ2 and Crystal City workforce. (Shuttle connection; no dock at National Landing.)
sections.timing: Targeting first service no earlier than end-2027. Every travel time shown is indicative until routes are finalized with harbor authorities.
sections.loi_ask: Register interest with a non-binding letter of intent. It costs nothing and reserves nothing — it tells us which corridors to launch first.
